name: Hadron structure and spectroscopy
observables: parton distribution functions and the d-bar/u-bar sea asymmetry
polarised structure functions and spin asymmetries (gluon and quark spin contributions)
generalised parton distributions (deeply virtual Compton scattering)
elastic form factors and the proton charge radius
meson and baryon masses, widths and J^PC quantum numbers
exotic candidates: tetraquarks, pentaquarks, hybrids, glueballs
parity-violating asymmetries (weak charge of the proton, neutron skin)
overview: Hadron structure and spectroscopy asks how the strongly interacting particles arise from quarks and gluons. Structure experiments scatter electrons, muons and hadron beams off nucleons and nuclei to map their momentum, spatial and spin structure; the proton spin puzzle and the transverse structure of the nucleon remain central open questions. The planned Electron-Ion Collider is designed to collide high-energy electron beams with proton and ion beams, reaching the regions of nucleons and nuclei where structure is dominated by gluons, and polarized beams give access to the spatial and spin structure of the proton, neutron and light ions. Spectroscopy tests whether QCD's allowed exotic states exist beyond the quark-antiquark and three-quark scheme: tetraquarks, pentaquarks, hybrids with active gluonic degrees of freedom and glueballs, and a 2019 review counted many new hadrons, found in the preceding fifteen years in the quarkonium spectrum, that do not match the expected properties of ordinary states. Parity-violating electron scattering, in which the parity-violating asymmetry isolates the weak interaction, measures the weak charge of the proton and the neutron skin of heavy nuclei, linking this topic to precision electroweak tests.
question: How are protons, neutrons and other hadrons built from quarks and gluons - where do their spin and size come from, and which exotic combinations of quarks and gluons exist?
